raw_response:
I am old now, and my land is not much, just 13.1 mu, so I do not fool around with fancy changes. I have done wheat-maize for many years. What worked last year, I mostly follow this year too. If I put too little fertilizer, the crop shows it right away and I lose more than the saved money. But I also cannot spend too hard, because only two people are in the house and cash must stay in hand. I have a well, so for wheat I will still water a few times, especially before winter and around jointing if the land is dry. Maize depends more on the rain, but if it turns dry in summer, I will give one or two irrigations. I use seed from the local dealer, the kind everybody nearby uses. I do not chase the most expensive one, just the one that is steady.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after I clear the maize. I usually put basal fertilizer first, then give another topdressing when the wheat starts to stand up strong in spring. For maize, the time is tight after wheat harvest, so I do it fast, with simple field prep and quick sowing. I would rather keep the land turning smoothly than lose days in the middle. My main thought is this: steady harvest is better than taking risk. At my age, I want the crop to come in safely, not to gamble for a little more.
